title: threads
description: Scrapes posts, and optionally replies, from a public Threads profile or tag. NEEDS NO ACCOUNT AND NO SIGN-IN: Threads serves this data to anyone, so there is nothing to connect and nothing to expire. A date range is a window the run must COVER, not merely filter to: with start_date/end_date and no max_posts, the run collects every post in the range and reports whether it managed to cover it.

target.description: A profile ('lumen', '@lumen' or a threads.com/... URL) or, in tag mode, a tag ('#space' or 'space').

mode.description: What the target names. Defaults to 'profile'. A TAG feed is served in ONE SHOT - it cannot be paged anonymously - so max_posts and a date range can only narrow what that single response happened to carry. A profile feed pages properly and is strictly reverse-chronological, so a date range genuinely covers a period there.

max_posts.description: Cap on posts returned. Threads caps a page at 25 server-side, so larger numbers mean more requests rather than bigger ones. OMIT IT when using a date range on a profile: the range is then the stopping condition.

start_date.description: Only posts at or after this moment (UTC, inclusive). A bare date means midnight.

end_date.description: Only posts at or before this moment (UTC, inclusive). A bare date means end of day.

collect_comments.description: Also collect each post's replies. THE PUBLIC CEILING IS REAL: logged out, Threads serves only about 5-10% of a post's replies (measured 21 of 365, 27 of 973, 26 of 477) with no way to page further, so asking for more than ~30 returns the same ~26 and costs nothing extra. Each post records how many it was actually served, so a short count is never mistaken for a failure.

max_comments_per_post.description: Cap on replies per post. With a connected Threads account every reply is reachable up to this cap; without one Threads serves only ~10-26 per post (measured ~10 in late September 2026) and higher values change nothing - see collect_comments.

analyse.description: Also produce an AI analysis and report (text, PDF and an HTML dashboard) alongside the data. Defaults to true. Costs two Claude calls; the scrape itself is unaffected either way.

ai_prompt.description: Your own analysis instructions, e.g. 'focus on complaints about delivery times'. Added to the built-in brief rather than replacing it, so the report keeps its structure and always renders.
